\[
9984=2^8\cdot 3\cdot 13
\]

For any divisor \(d\) of \(9984\) with \(d>15\), the next multiple is \(9984+d>9999\), so \(9984\) remains the largest 4-digit multiple.

Divisors of \(9984\) that are \(\le 15\) are \(1,2,3,4,6,8,12,13\), and each fails (e.g. \(13\mid 9997\), \(12\mid 9996\)).

Thus the divisor is not unique; any divisor of \(9984\) greater than \(15\) works, such as \(16,24,32,\ldots\)

\[
\boxed{\text{Not unique; any divisor of }9984>15\text{ works}}
\]
